lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: CHAPTER 36
lines.note: Chapter heading.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The Fourth Mark
lines.note: Chapter title. Leave a clean beat before story begins.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The left-hand passage opened into a chamber that held a silence so absolute it felt like a physical object—something with weight and edges that had settled into the room ahead of them and simply refused to leave.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek raised the torch.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Two marks already occupied the far wall.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The lower one was nearly erased by centuries until it barely resembled a loop at all—more suggestion than symbol, the way a word worn smooth on a gravestone becomes more shape than language. The middle one was clearer, filled with slime and age, its angles deliberate, as though whoever carved it had learned something from a mistake they could no longer remember making.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun stepped closer, fingers hovering above the stone without touching it.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: These are not the incomplete spirals,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: she said.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: These are attempts.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The journal opened in Zeek's hands before he reached for it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: THIS IS THE THIRD TIME YOU HAVE READ THIS.
lines.note: Written text (ledger/inscription/journal, not in Bel-iddin's hand). Cold, deliberate read.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He stared at the line. Then at the two marks. Then at the blank space above them.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg stood near the entrance, axe ready.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: Whatever you're reading into those scratches, make it quick. The passage we came through is starting to close.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-HEH-doo studied the wall with the remote attention she now gave anything that could not be priced.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: Two versions of the same decision. Or two people making the same decision and calling it different names.
lines.note: Post-vision (Ch.29+): same voice, flattened affect. Even pitch, slower, no reach.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek understood what the journal required of him the way he had once understood the price of a trap before placing his foot.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He took out his knife.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The third mark was cut with a kind of desperate precision he recognized in his own aching fingers even as he made it. The lines were cleaner than the oldest attempt, less confident than the middle one. When he stepped back, the three carvings stood in a vertical line: crude, deliberate, desperate.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: The oldest is the first attempt,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: he said. His voice sounded hollow against the stone.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: The middle one is the second. And the one I just carved—that was supposed to be the third.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun's torchlight moved over the stone in slow arcs.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: But the journal said this is the third time you have read this. Not the fourth. The third.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The logic assembled itself with a speed that felt almost cruel.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: If the journal claimed this was the third reading, and the wall already held three marks—two older than his own—then either the journal was counting something different from the carvings, or the carvings recorded attempts the journal refused to acknowledge.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Or both.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: As they watched, the newest mark began to darken. The pale edges took on the same aged sheen as the middle carving. The stone was absorbing the cut, folding the fresh wound into its history as if the act of carving had never been new.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun tried to copy the oldest mark. The ink refused to hold. The line appeared, then faded, then appeared again in a slightly different shape.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: It's rewriting itself while I watch.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Above Zeek's own mark a fourth position began to form—not a carving yet, only a faint discoloration in the stone, the ghost of a place where something had once been, or would be.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: There's a fourth,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: he said.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun followed his gaze.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: I don't see it.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: Not yet.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The discoloration deepened. A thin line appeared, then another. The shape assembling itself was not a knot. It was something else entirely: a vertical line descending into a small open circle.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek's palm burned.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The journal opened again.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: THE FOURTH PLACE IS YOURS.
lines.note: Written text (ledger/inscription/journal, not in Bel-iddin's hand). Cold, deliberate read.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek's blood went cold.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun looked at him, her voice barely above a whisper.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: Then whose is the mark already forming?
lines.note: Whispered.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He had no answer that was not another transaction.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The chamber went completely dark.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Not gradually. Not as though the torches had failed. Darkness arrived all at once, as though something had reached into the room and closed a hand around every flame.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek heard Ninsun inhale sharply beside him. The sound seemed unnaturally loud in the sudden absence of light.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Then, somewhere beyond the wall, something knocked.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Three measured blows.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A pause.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Then a fourth.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek tightened his grip on the journal. The leather felt warm beneath his fingers.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: We need to go.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: Where?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg asked.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek couldn't see the wall anymore, but he could still feel it, the way a man knows where a doorway stands in a familiar room even with his eyes closed.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: The knocking.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: No one argued.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They followed the sound because it was the only direction the darkness had left them.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek walked first, one hand sliding along damp stone, the journal pressed beneath his arm. Behind him he heard Ninsun's footsteps falter only once.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Not from fear.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: From hesitation.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: As though she had already begun wondering whether they had left something unfinished.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: I'd like it recorded,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg said.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: That I objected to following the invisible thing that knocks.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: You didn't object,
lines.note: Post-vision (Ch.29+): same voice, flattened affect. Even pitch, slower, no reach.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-HEH-doo said.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: You raised the torch and went first.
lines.note: Post-vision (Ch.29+): same voice, flattened affect. Even pitch, slower, no reach.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: I objected internally.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: That seems convenient.
lines.note: Post-vision (Ch.29+): same voice, flattened affect. Even pitch, slower, no reach.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: It saves time. Imagine how slow we'd move if I explained every damn sensible thought I had.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-HEH-doo's mouth shifted at one corner.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: I've never had to imagine that.
lines.note: Post-vision (Ch.29+): same voice, flattened affect. Even pitch, slower, no reach.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek's thumb crossed the scar in his palm. The pressure behind his eyes had diminished after they left the chamber, though it had not vanished. It waited behind his thoughts like the last note of a struck bell, too low to hear but still present in the bone.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Behind them came the soft mineral sigh of stone settling into stillness.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek resisted the urge to look back.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Somehow he knew the fourth mark remained where they had left it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Not completed.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Waiting.
